data.title: Bitcoin buyers make a play off swing area support.  What do buyers have to do to increase upside potential?
data.description:
Bitcoin fell to a low of $61,947 on Sunday, November 15 and bounced but the bounce was somewhat modest to $66069 before sellers returned.  Those sellers took the price back to the Sunday low, and nearly matched it on late  Wednesday. However, the price decline once again ran into willing buyers within the four-hour swing area floor between $61,183 and $62,470 (see red numbered circles on the chart below).

That second test gave buyers another opportunity to lean against the old floor. The near-double bottom at $61,947 gave them a nearby level to define and limit risk, and the rebound has taken the price back to $63,864.

data.title: Morning Kickstart. Nasdaq futures rally ahead of Anthropic’s debut as yields climb
data.description:
Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its $70 to $78 range, and Nasdaq futures are leading the rebound this morning. The public offering totaled $81.3 billion, or $107.3 billion including the private placement, at a fully diluted valuation of roughly $1.5 trillion. Gray-market indications pointed to an opening roughly 20% to 26% above the offer price. ANT is due to start trading on Nasdaq today, with the first trade coming once the exchange’s opening auction establishes a price. There’s no set time.

There’s plenty of growth behind the demand. Anthropic reported $33.2 billion in revenue through September, up from $2.5 billion a year earlier, and put its October annualized revenue run rate at about $81 billion. The nine-month net loss was about $104 billion, driven largely by financing-related fair-value changes. The operating loss was $1.3 billion. Once ANT opens, I’ll be watching whether it holds its opening gains and whether the chip and cloud stocks hold theirs. That will tell us more about demand for the broader AI trade than the opening print alone. ipo.anthropic.com

data.title: Suckers' rally 2.0? Nasdaq rebounds amid Anthropic enthusiasm despite growing macro risks
data.description:
The Nasdaq's suckers' rally, which I discussed in a previous article, eventually erased all the gains and retested the monthly lows. We are now seeing another recovery despite an even more hawkish Fed and no changes in the Middle East tensions.

I think this is another suckers’ rally which is probably being driven by Anthropic enthusiasm. The stock will start trading today on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, although there’s no confirmed opening time.

data.title: Project to support underprivileged students completed, Elev8 broker reports
data.description:
Throughout October 2026, Elev8, a global broker, ran a charity initiative called Charity October, setting aside a fixed amount for every lot its clients traded. Elev8 covered the entire donation budget, clients didn't contribute anything, and participation was free for all.

At the end of the month, the funds were transferred to Elev8's partner, JAAGO Foundation, a Bangladesh-based non-profit that supports local communities and promotes education among underserved populations.

data.title: Solana's downtrend remains intact despite easing selling pressure. What could change the picture?
data.description:
Solana has been recovering some losses as the selling momentum waned amid lack of further bearish catalysts. However, the bearish trend remains intact, with the more hawkish Fed, the US-Iran stalemate and growing concerns about the global growth outlook continuing to weigh on risk sentiment.

There are no major catalysts left for this week. Unless we get some unscheduled geopolitical or macro development, the recovery might extend further.

data.title: Crude oil extends losses amid growth concerns but risk of US strikes keeps the downside limited
data.description:
Crude oil extended the losses yesterday, with growth concerns looking increasingly as the likely culprit given no change on the US-Iran front.

In fact, the Middle East tensions remain elevated, with the risk of further escalation increasing. Trump is reportedly weighing new strikes on Iran while insisting that the US does not need outside help and that the blockade remains its most effective tool. US officials also warned that Iran is prepared for further escalation and Israel is pushing for action.

data.title: Ethereum consolidates around recent lows as the bearish momentum wanes amid lack of catalysts
data.description:
Ethereum has been consolidating around recent lows as the selling momentum eased. However, the bearish drivers remain in place amid the more hawkish Fed, the US-Iran stalemate and growth concerns.

The week is basically over, and we don’t have key catalysts on the agenda. Unless we get some unscheduled major news, the rangebound price action might extend further.

data.title: Gold's selloff may be nearing exhaustion as growth concerns challenge hawkish expectations
data.description:
Gold extended the selloff further yesterday despite no fresh catalyst. We only had Fed’s Waller reaffirming his case for a more aggressive action to break the inflationary mindset, but that wasn’t something new.

As things stand, the Fed is widely expected to hike by 25 bps at the next meeting in December and deliver at least three rate hikes in total by the end of 2027. I think the hawkish repricing should now be mostly over, so the risk to reward for more downside at current levels isn’t ideal.

data.title: GTA VI lifts Sony shares as PlayStation takes three-quarters of 17 million sales
data.description:
Sony’s nearly 3% gain stood out against a flat TOPIX and a week of AI-driven selling in Japanese tech, so the stock may attract buyers looking for growth away from the chip theme. Early sales figures give Take-Two some support heading into the US session, while Microsoft’s Xbox looks a distant second on the platform split. The memory cost angle connects to the wider AI story. Chipmakers such as Samsung and SK Hynix benefit from tight supply, while device makers like Sony feel the squeeze, which pushes them toward software and royalties. Nintendo shares are unlikely to suffer, given its separate hit in Japan.

---

data.title: Goldman cuts KOSPI target to 7,500 but says gloom is overdone, sees 48% upside
data.description:
Goldman’s move is a lower target with a bullish message, and that mix explains Thursday’s price action: chip stocks dipped early, then buyers stepped in. Its argument that memory stocks already price in a 70% earnings cut gives dip-buyers a framework, but the AI sentiment shock from Nvidia means volatility in Samsung and SK Hynix is likely to persist. The non-chip angle matters most for flows. If governance reforms and buybacks hold up, financials and other low-valuation sectors could draw rotation money away from semiconductors. Light foreign positioning also means any improvement in AI sentiment could lift the index quickly.

---

data.title: ETH whales keep buying through the slide while bitcoin whales send coins to exchanges
data.description: If the split in whale behaviour persists, ETH could hold up better than bitcoin, and that would show first in the ETH/BTC ratio. Buying through trading desks doesn’t show up in spot ETF data, so it can run alongside weak fund flows: US spot bitcoin ETFs lost roughly $2.1 billion between late October and mid-November. Continued net deposits by bitcoin whales leave BTC rallies exposed to fresh supply, a headwind for crypto equities such as COIN and listed miners, which tend to follow the bitcoin price. For wider risk sentiment, steady ETH buying at around $1,765 suggests some large buyers see value after the drop.
